title: A node's clock jumps 10 minutes ahead
teaches: munge credentials are only valid within ~5 minutes; clock skew is an auth failure in disguise.

events.text: chrony stopped on slurm-c1; clock +10 min
not responding: clock: slurm-c1 -> investigate/critical/unreachable (want investigate) OK

data.summary: slurmd stopped responding. If the host is up, restart slurmd before SlurmdTimeout marks the node DOWN.

chrony started and stepped the clock; slurmd restarted

got.summary: slurmd stopped responding. If the host is up, restart slurmd before SlurmdTimeout marks the node DOWN.

commands: ssh slurm-c1 'sudo systemctl restart slurmd && journalctl -u slurmd -n 20'
evidence: state IDLE+NOT_RESPONDING; CPUs 0/2 allocated; GRES gpu:fake:4 (in use: gpu:fake:0(IDX:N/A))
next_steps: Check whether the host is reachable at all.
If it is, restart slurmd; running jobs survive a slurmd restart.
If the host is gone, the jobs are already lost. Let the timeout mark it DOWN and follow the down-node path.
